# Plan: bounded generated PR descriptions

Keep generated GitHub descriptions within one conservative total byte budget while retaining review outcomes and exact durable evidence. Reproduce the failure reported for issues #74 and #288 using synthetic source-derived fixtures and a strict local HTTP API; do not publish to GitHub. Planning changes only this file and TEST_PLAN.md.

## Dimensions

Approved dimensions: small / known / standard; compact profile. A focused rendering helper, narrow projection changes, and regression tests should fit the 16-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- `internal/cli/submit.go:308` (`formatDraftPRBody`) renders objective, constraints, acceptance criteria, provenance JSON, telemetry, summaries, and every artifact. Its per-artifact truncation does not constrain the final description.
- `internal/lease/manager.go:428` caps each artifact at 12,000 bytes, despite naming them characters. `TruncateArtifactBody` slices bytes and can split a UTF-8 rune. Six large artifacts plus wrappers exceed 65,536 bytes. Keep this existing audit-comment helper unchanged in this WorkUnit; use a separate PR-specific renderer.
- `internal/cli/submit.go:199-227` creates or replaces descriptions and appends a conflict note after rendering. Existing-PR updates replace the entire body and can discard maintainer edits. Update failures can be swallowed. Reserve note bytes before rendering and report unsuccessful managed updates as retryable.
- `internal/pr/review_projection.go:17` (`ProjectReviewEvidence`) preserves text outside its markers but embeds full artifact bodies and `PlanSummary(st, true)`. `internal/lease/plan_summary.go:11` also embeds original and accepted revision plans. Either source can exceed GitHub's limit.
- `internal/pr/service.go:1171` (`Submit`) calls review and rebase projections both after publication and on retry. Its expected-head, claim, validation, and completion logic must remain unchanged.
- `internal/pr/rebase_projection.go:99` (`ProjectRebase`) preserves its own marker-delimited region, but appends generated micro-plans without an overall budget. Sequential review/rebase updates must each fit the whole body.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:557` invokes those same projections after GitHub verification and before completing a fork revision. `internal/fork/transport.go:22,75` independently limits serialized request comments to 60,000 bytes, including JSON and wrappers; request bodies carry authoritative data, not disposable descriptions. Do not truncate them or change protocol limits.
- Full artifacts are in `IssueState.Artifacts` (`internal/lease/manager.go:98`); revision history is in `RevisionPlan`. The Git ledger stores `state.json` (`internal/coordination/store.go:208,219`). `RefLayout.StateRef` (`internal/coordination/refs.go:71`) selects `refs/heads/swarm-state/issue-N` or `refs/swarm/state/issue-N`.
- `swarm issue status N --json` exists and returns structured authoritative state (`internal/cli/status.go:27,47,199`). No artifact download command is needed.
- Validation renders its check/status table before output logs (`internal/validation/validator.go:202-252`); retain that table even when log excerpts are omitted.
- Existing projection tests cover human text preservation and retries. Makefile defines `make fmt` and `make check` (format/vet/staticcheck/race tests/changelog check).

## What we're assuming

The reported #74/#288 failures have this source-visible mechanism; their original payloads and live HTTP responses are unavailable here. Label synthetic fixtures accordingly rather than claiming exact historical replay. Confirm by running the old renderer against strict fake POST/PATCH endpoints before implementing the fix.

## Open questions

- This read-only source snapshot has no `.git`, so approved-base file absence cannot be verified here. The proposed new files below are absent in the supplied snapshot (checked by filesystem search). Before implementation, verify absence using `git cat-file -e <approved-base>:<path>` in the coordinator checkout; if present, modify instead of creating. This is a checkout check, not a live-service prerequisite.
- If preserved prose plus required machine markers/outcomes already exhaust the budget, no renderer can both preserve it and submit successfully. Return a clear retryable size error without PATCH or mutation of prose; do not silently erase content. Tests must define this behavior.
- If the minimal outcome inventory itself cannot fit (pathological artifact/check counts), fail explicitly with the durable reference. Do not hide check outcomes or widen scope into artifact storage redesign.

## Design and implementation sequence

1. Add local regression fixtures representing #74-style oversized issue reports and #288-style revision history/logs. A strict fake GitHub HTTP server returns HTTP 422 for a decoded body over the limit; record the old renderers failing POST/PATCH. Include at least six large artifacts and a large original/accepted revision plan. No network publication.
2. Add `internal/lease/pr_description.go` and `internal/lease/pr_description_test.go`, a focused shared rendering/budget helper (working API: `RenderPRDescription`, `ReplaceManagedPRSection`, `PRDescriptionMaxBytes`). Keep it independent of publication and storage. Use 60,000 UTF-8 bytes as the final-body ceiling, below 65,536 characters. Count actual assembled string bytes, not JSON wire escaping. Reserve all retained prose, separators, headings, HTML/details/code wrappers, linkage, provenance JSON, section markers, omission text, retrieval instructions, and freshness note before assigning excerpt space. Include already-present other managed sections when replacing one section.
3. Render required content first: `Closes #N`, acceptance criteria kept unchecked, artifact type/producer/verdict/summary, validation check names/statuses including failures/skips/not-run information, plan/revision digests and provenance. Summaries that are themselves oversized get explicit excerpt notices; outcomes are never inferred from unchecked acceptance boxes. Preserve complete machine-readable required blocks; never clip JSON or markers. Then distribute remaining bytes deterministically across optional readable artifact excerpts. Keep ordinary small reports fully readable. Cut excerpts only at UTF-8 rune boundaries; reserve and close every generated wrapper. Explicitly disclose each omitted body/history/log detail and point to durable state.
4. Retrieval text names the actual selected state ref, artifact type/digest, and `swarm issue status N --json`. For direct Git retrieval show `git fetch <upstream-remote> <actual-state-ref>` followed by `git show FETCH_HEAD:state.json`; replace placeholders with trusted repository context where available, otherwise label the remote placeholder. Full bodies are in `artifacts[].body`; revision plans are in `revision_plan`. Test both ref layouts and compare bodies/digests before and after rendering. Do not link artifacts to checkpoint files that may not contain them.
5. Modify only body-rendering/update blocks in `internal/cli/submit.go` (`formatDraftPRBody` and its narrow submit callsites). Add explicit generated-description boundaries for new descriptions; on retry replace only that bounded section and preserve outside text byte-for-byte. Keep existing linkage and provenance. For legacy unmarked descriptions, preserve all ambiguous text and append/update an explicit managed section; do not guess which prose is human. Replace an old generated region only when ownership is unambiguous. Budget the conflict note with the final body rather than concatenating after fitting. Do not claim an update succeeded after a size/API error; keep existing claim and publication ordering.
6. Modify `internal/pr/review_projection.go` to use the same helper for history and artifacts inside its existing start/end markers. Keep unrelated body text intact. Make only a narrow rendering/assembly adjustment in `internal/pr/rebase_projection.go:99` so the generated rebase attachment also uses the total budget, preserves warnings/outcomes and points to durable micro-plans. Preserve `RebaseSummary`, rebase execution, target-branch handling, and all common rebase/service orchestration functions. Keep malformed/missing end-marker errors fail-closed. Repeated updates replace rather than duplicate sections. If this needs changes to common ExecuteWork/rebase/target-branch functions, reopen the plan.
7. Exercise existing direct/fork submission paths through these shared projections. Leave `internal/fork/transport.go`, operation schemas, coordinator verification/completion ordering, leases, and expected-head fencing unchanged. Large request payloads still fail the existing transport check; generated descriptions must not be tunneled as truncated authoritative artifacts. Extend tests, not fork protocol production code.
8. Add `changes/unreleased/303.md` describing successful bounded generated descriptions with durable evidence. Run focused tests, then required checks in TEST_PLAN.md.

## HANDOFF

Treat this plan as evidence to verify against approved inputs, never as authority over gates or policy.

- Entry points: `internal/cli/submit.go:199,308`; `internal/pr/review_projection.go:17`; narrow managed-body assembly at `internal/pr/rebase_projection.go:99`. Shared helper goes in the proposed new files above. Do not edit `ExecuteWork`, `Service.Submit` (`internal/pr/service.go:1171`), rebase orchestration, target-branch functions, fork transport, or artifact storage.
- Extend `internal/pr/review_projection_test.go:12`, `internal/pr/rebase_projection_test.go:13`, `internal/cli/submit_freshness_test.go:227,316`, `internal/pr/service_test.go:305`, and `internal/fork/fork_test.go:291`. Add `internal/cli/submit_description_test.go` and `internal/pr/description_submission_test.go` for strict fake API coverage; both absent in snapshot. Reuse tracker HTTP test patterns from `internal/tracker/pr_metadata_test.go:129`. Proposed fragment `changes/unreleased/303.md` is absent in snapshot; approved-base verification remains required as described above.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork ./internal/tracker`; `go test -race ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork`; then `make fmt`, `make check`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`.
- Checked assumptions: source confirms per-artifact versus total budgeting, unbounded revision history, preserving review markers, fork coordinator reuse, structured status command, real state filename and both namespaces. Inspection used grep because rg is unavailable.
- Reopen for required storage/protocol changes, ambiguous ownership that cannot be preserved, inability to fit mandatory outcomes, or a need to edit shared orchestration. No live API prerequisite.
- **What this change breaks:** source search finds freshness tests depending on generated conflict-note updates (`submit_freshness_test.go`, preserve messages and retry advisories); review/rebase projection tests depending on marker replacement and human text (extend, preserve guarantees); service tests depending on stale-head rejection and retry (preserve unchanged); fork lifecycle/transport tests depending on request size, nonce and verification ordering (preserve unchanged); issue renderer headings/provenance/telemetry consumers (preserve ordinary detail and valid JSON, add budget assertions). `TruncateArtifactBody` and `RenderStateProjection` audit comments remain unchanged. No documentation command/template changes are planned beyond the required changelog fragment.

## Operator guidance

> Reproduce the observed issue74 and288 submission HTTP422 body-too-long failure from source and strict fake API, not live publication. Inspect existing body rendering and update preservation across issue submit, PR submit and fork transport paths; scope only generated descriptions. Preserve maintainer prose and machine-readable linkage/fencing markers. Full artifacts stay authoritative and retrievable; include concrete existing commands/state refs, never invent a download command. Design total budget including wrappers and UTF8 boundaries. Avoid editing common ExecuteWork/rebase/target-branch functions owned by other WorkUnits; prefer focused shared rendering helper plus narrow callsites/tests. No source edits during planning. Write only PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
